doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Cab Calloway's band: road, arrangers and shows
title: Gershwin's ties to Harlem musicians, Will Vodery and singer Edith Wilson
summary: Hinton says the Harlem connection to Gershwin goes unmentioned, recalls Gershwin taking a Chicago singer to Paris and interviewing Edith Wilson.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: That‟s right. He used to sit around and rehearse for Fletcher because Fletcher would have a rehearsal and he‟d be making another arrangement. So he was in Harlem and involved in it. The same thing with Gershwin see… how can you write about people like Catfish [unintelligible] unless you had some really contact. And of course nobody mentions this nowadays but if you know somebody like I know, like I mentioned to you when he was still living, Will Foger… see he was just copying. He was sitting in that orchestra under Will Foger. Well that don‟t sit too good for us to be mentioned in that line. And then there‟s a lady from Chicago that just passed a couple of years ago, black lady, a beautiful singer. I‟ll ask Mona to tell you her name. She came to New York and did that show at Town Hall. Gershwin took her to Paris with him because he was having a lot [unintelligible]. I‟ve got some tapes down there of the songs that he wrote for her in Paris.
You want to stop the tape just a second?
Yeah, so it‟s not too chic to mention that kind of thing in particulars circles, although Gershwin…

It‟s the truth and in Gershwin‟s book there‟s a picture… I think I have one of his books downstairs, a book of his life with a picture of Venus Wilson in his book. It doesn‟t say what that close connection…
I had no idea. I know she was close to Huby Blake. She and many of those ladies that were really the top singers for the shows and all that stuff, they were wonderful.
Like everybody wanted to write for them because of the manner in which they projected the song.

Yeah. Well I was so thrilled to be in that show down there, to get a chance to interview Edith Wilson. She was kind of ill then and Mona was trying to be very nice to her and take care of her. Atley Hall and that lady was in good spirits and I got to talk to them. I got to talk to her about her trip to Paris with George Gershwin and she sang a couple of songs for me that he wrote for her. I haven‟t heard any of these particular songs lately. And then this other lady that… Love For Sale, I don‟t even know who wrote Love For Sale.

It was written for this lady and she was there too. It‟s amazing to find out [unintelligible] check these things out. I‟m not talking about sending somebody a ghostly whisper but I talked to Harold Aland and I talked to Will Foger.
Right, and they say that, sure.
